claims.text: The Dependency Inversion Principle: high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry dip; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: OrderPlacedTightlyCoupled has a field `private readonly EmailNotifier notifier = new();` and Handle calls notifier.Send(orderId, "order placed"); OrderNotifications takes an INotifier constructor parameter and has an identical Handle.
OrderService (DonHang.Domain) takes IOrderRepository and INotifier as constructor parameters and PlaceOrderAsync calls notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"); it never names a concrete notifier.
INotifier used by OrderService is declared in DonHang.Domain (DonHang.Domain/INotifier.cs); LoggingNotifier in DonHang.Infrastructure implements it by logging.
DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj references DonHang.Domain; DonHang.Domain.csproj has no ProjectReference.

A C# constructor parameter typed INotifier accepts an instance of any class implementing INotifier (implicit reference conversion), so callers can pass EmailNotifier, SmsNotifier or a new implementation without the receiving class changing.
claims.source_hint: C# conversions: implicit reference conversion from class to implemented interface

claims.text: A class implementing an interface must provide an implementation for every member the interface declares, so changing a declared member such as Send's parameters forces a change in the implementing class (here NotifierBase, through which EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier implement INotifier).
claims.source_hint: C# interfaces: implementing members must match the interface member signature

claims.text: High-level code that creates new EmailNotifier() itself is tied to EmailNotifier even if it stores the result in an INotifier variable.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; coupling definition from design.l1.coupling-and-cohesion

claims.text: DIP concerns the direction of dependencies; the mechanism that creates concrete objects and passes them in is a separate topic (next module).
